game_updates.title: Upcoming Changes to X4: Foundations Minimum System Requirements
game_updates.contents: As we continue to develop and expand X4: Foundations, we are constantly looking for ways to improve the game's proprietary engine and overall performance. To keep pushing the boundaries of what our engine can do, we are preparing to upgrade our graphics API to Vulkan 1.4 as part of a future update. Our plan is to do this as part of the next major update after 9.00. Because of this necessary technological step forward, we will soon be updating the minimum GPU requirements for X4: Foundations. Why are we making this change? Transitioning to Vulkan 1.4 is a significant technical milestone for us. As a small team, splitting our resources between legacy hardware support and modern development has become a significant drain; continuing to support older hardware requires us to maintain more code,...

game_updates.title: Wallpaper Engine 2.8.42 - Removal of Application Wallpapers from the Workshop
game_updates.contents: Hey everyone, this update introduces a security change to Wallpaper Engine. In the next week, we will be permanently removing the "Application" wallpaper type from the public Steam Workshop. While this sounds drastic, it affects merely 0.5% of all wallpapers with actual user numbers being much lower than even that. The overwhelming majority of users never used any applications wallpapers at all, since they are hidden by default in the app. As part of this transition, we are currently cleaning up the Workshop. Most application wallpapers will start to be set to friends-only for the transition period. If there are any Application-type wallpapers you actively use and want to keep, you have a grace period of around one week to back them up locally. Why did Application Wallpapers exist in the f...

game_updates.title: Payday 2's next update is "a massive undertaking" to modernize the FPS, stop crashes, and cut its install size by 60%
game_updates.contents: It's been nine months since Starbreeze handed the Payday 2 reins over to Sidetrack Games to continue supporting it, while the original developer focused on improving Payday 3. So far, the numbers are very much in Sidetrack's favor, with Payday 2 still routinely pulling 30,000-player peaks on Steam as its successor struggles to stay at just 1,000. Rather than simply rest easy, however, the new team is preparing for its biggest overhaul yet, transporting the heist shooter across to a fresh engine that should result in smoother gameplay at a massively reduced file size. Read the full story on PCGamesN: Payday 2's next update is "a massive undertaking" to modernize the FPS, stop crashes, and cut its install size by 60%
